task_production_rates.name: Sand primed surface 220 grit before grain fill
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr for flat surface baseline. 220 grit orbital on flats, hand on profiles. Standard prep sanding rate on already-primed surface. Binary. Apply surface_profile modifier.

task_production_rates.name: Apply grain filler skim coat
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr for flat surface baseline. Blended flat/profile application — squeegee on flats forcing filler into grain pores, brush on profiles. Wipe excess off cross-grain. qt_scaled — rate is per-coat, coat count driven by QT (1/2/3). Apply surface_profile and wood_species modifiers.

task_production_rates.name: Sand between fill coats
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr for flat surface baseline. 220-320 grit depending on coat number. Orbital on flats, hand on profiles. qt_scaled — matches fill coat count. Apply surface_profile and wood_species modifiers.

task_production_rates.name: Final sand 400 grit (QT5 only)
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr for flat surface baseline. 400 grit hand work only — no orbital at this grit. Glass-smooth surface prep. QT5 only. Binary (runs once when QT5). Apply surface_profile modifier. Wood_species modifier does NOT apply (sanding filled surface, not filling grain).

task_production_rates.name: Apply second prime coat (seal coat over filler)
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr for flat surface baseline. Standard primer application rate — seal coat is a normal primer coat. Uses parent spec's primer product. Binary. Apply surface_profile modifier. Wood_species modifier does NOT apply (priming, not filling grain).

task_production_rates.name: Sand second prime 320 grit
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr for flat surface baseline. 320 grit light sand for finish coat adhesion tooth. Orbital on flats, hand on profiles. Binary. Apply surface_profile modifier. Wood_species modifier does NOT apply.

surface_profile_modifier.application_rule: Modifiers increase TIME. effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. Apply to ALL SF-based tasks. Profiled surfaces require hand work where flat surfaces can use squeegee/orbital. Heavy_profile is the dominant cost driver in this spec.
surface_profile_modifier.notes: flat=cabinet doors, flat trim, flat panels. light_profile=simple casing, baseboard with small profile. medium_profile=crown molding, chair rail, standard raised panel. heavy_profile=ornate crown, complex raised panel, dentil trim.

wood_species_modifier.application_rule: Modifiers increase TIME. effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. Apply ONLY to TSK_GRAIN_FILL_COAT and TSK_GRAIN_SAND_BETWEEN. Does NOT apply to TSK_GRAIN_FINAL_SAND, TSK_GRAIN_PRIME_SEAL, or TSK_GRAIN_SAND_PRIME (these tasks work on filled/primed surface, not raw grain).
wood_species_modifier.notes: deep_grain=oak, hickory (baseline — most common grain fill substrate). moderate_grain=ash, walnut (shallower grain, faster fill). Modifier makes moderate_grain FASTER than deep_grain (0.85x means effective_rate = base / 0.85 = higher rate).

height_modifiers.application_rule: Modifiers increase TIME. effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. Apply to ALL tasks. Standard height modifiers — grain fill work height depends on the substrate being filled.

estimation_notes.sf_based: All 6 tasks use SF as primary UOM. SF from PaintScope input PS_SURFACE_SF.GRAIN_FILL (pre-converted from parent substrate UOM).
estimation_notes.surface_profile_dominance: Surface profile is the dominant modifier. A heavy_profile surface (crown molding, 2.8x) takes nearly 3x as long as a flat surface (cabinet door, 1.0x). This reflects the reality that grain fill on profiled surfaces requires meticulous hand work on every contour.
estimation_notes.modifier_stacking: Max theoretical stacking: heavy_profile (2.8) × H3 (1.5) × deep_grain (1.0) = 4.2x. This exceeds the 4.0x flag threshold. Realistic worst case: heavy_profile crown molding at 13+ ft height with deep-grain oak. Flag for review but likely accurate — this is genuinely very slow work.
estimation_notes.wood_species_selective: Wood species modifier only applies to fill coat and sand between tasks — these are the tasks where grain depth directly affects production rate. Second prime and its sanding are normal coating operations unaffected by grain depth.
estimation_notes.no_dry_times: Per RC-004: no dry times specified. AquaCoat grain filler typically dries in 30-60 minutes between coats. Refer to product TDS.
estimation_notes.add_on_cost_structure: Grain fill adds significant cost to the parent spec. Example: QT4 grain fill on 100 SF of flat oak trim = ~3.3 hours (sand prep 1h + 2 fill coats @ 1.4h + 2 sand between @ 1.25h + prime seal 0.67h + sand prime 1.1h ÷ multiplied and adjusted). The cost is justified — grain fill transforms a textured surface into a glass-smooth finish.

assumptions.value: 70 SF/hr flat surface grain filler application
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides grain fill production rates. Squeegee + brush technique. Flat surface baseline.
Profile modifier values need field calibration. The jump from medium (2.0) to heavy (2.8) reflects exponential difficulty increase on ornate profiles.
Species modifier values need field calibration.

assumptions.source: Aligned with parent spec primer rates
assumptions.note: Second prime is a standard primer coat — uses existing primer rate.
